# Zen Mesh — Documentation Index

> Zen Mesh is private-by-design, security-first webhook delivery infrastructure for private networks. Services behind NAT or firewall connect outbound-only to receive webhooks from Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, Twilio, and custom senders — no inbound ports, no VPN, no kernel modules. Free for development and evaluation. 6-month Pro trial available. Business and Enterprise plans coming soon.

**Version:** 1.0 · **Last-Updated:** 2026-06-25 · **Docs:** https://docs.zen-mesh.io · **Site:** https://www.zen-mesh.io · **Repository:** https://github.com/zenmesh/zen-platform

## Getting started

- [Quick start](getting-started/quick-start): Sandbox-oriented setup — create endpoints, targets, flows, send test webhooks
- [Installation](getting-started/installation): Install paths for evaluation (Docker, Edge Lite binary, source)
- [First webhook](getting-started/first-webhook): Step-by-step first webhook walkthrough
- [Edge Lite](ai/edge-lite): Pre-launch design-partner evaluation mode — single-container Docker-based Zen Mesh Edge

## Pricing

- **Free Forever:** $0/month — 3 webhook endpoints, 25,000 webhooks/month, 256 KB max payload, 3 targets, 3 routes/flows, 7-day retention, shared receive IPs. Development and evaluation only — not for production use.
- **Pro — Early Bird:** $29/month (6-month free trial with monthly feedback survey; reference standard $49/month). 50 endpoints, 500,000 webhooks/month, 1 MB payload, 25 targets, 50 routes, 30-day retention, S3 log export, 1 seat. No SLA or dedicated IP.
- **Business:** Coming soon. Planned: dedicated receive IP add-on, higher limits, payload export and Object Lock, stronger liability posture.
- **Enterprise:** Contact zen@zen-mesh.io for custom pricing, SLAs, dedicated infrastructure, and compliance workflows.

See [plans and limits](start-here/plans-and-limits) and [site pricing](https://www.zen-mesh.io/pricing).

## Competitive positioning

Zen Mesh differentiates on private-network delivery. Most webhook tools assume the receiver has a public endpoint or uses polling/tunnels. Zen Mesh uses outbound-only connections (Edge Lite / zen-agent) so services behind NAT or firewall can receive webhooks without opening inbound ports, VPN, or kernel modules.

Additional differentiators:
- Docker-first / private-environment path: Start with Edge Lite; no Kubernetes required for evaluation
- Security-first webhook infrastructure: mTLS, SPIFFE/SPIRE, HMAC on every data-plane path — non-negotiable
- Verifiable delivery evidence: Hash-chain receipts and tamper-evident delivery logs
- Provider Template Packs: Reusable packages for Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, Twilio, and custom signed webhooks — structured defaults for endpoint setup, provider verification, event classification, and operational visibility. Optional, accelerate setup while preserving full user control.
- Kubernetes/cloud-native path: Full helm-based deployment for production environments
- Non-claims and gaps published alongside claims

## Security

- [Security posture](ai/security-posture): Claim maturity legend and reviewer highlights

- [ZenLock](zen-lock): Credential lifecycle management

- [Trust Lab](security/trust-lab): Deterministic validation scenarios for webhook delivery
- [Security Validation Suite](security/security-validation-suite): Adversarial and boundary validation
- 2FA/MFA is a V1 security prerequisite currently tracked as a blocker until runtime evidence lands. Local/password auth requires app-level 2FA for V1. OIDC MFA may be delegated to the identity provider for V1 when configured.
- [Security plan tiering](security/security-tiering): Feature availability by plan (V1 / V1.1)
- [Security features](security): TLS, mTLS, IP allowlisting, header validation, cryptographic enrollment
